title: The Generative Frontier of the Voynich Manuscript
summary: The author compares synthetic mechanisms with matched manuscript samples using local reuse, positional rigidity, entropy and lexical productivity. The study includes parameter-matched comparisons on disjoint folio sets and a cross-check against Parisel's published positional tests.
established: A reimplementation of Timm and Schinner's similar-glyph procedure gives conditional character entropy of 2.38 bits without fitting that statistic, close to the 2.34-bit EVA manuscript estimate. The study reports that the absolute estimate shifts under the v101 alphabet.

All of the tested matched generators passed the four Parisel positional signatures under the published verifier, including the grille example, limiting those tests' power to distinguish the mechanisms in this comparison.

The proposed stock-and-flow generator falls inside the study's three folio-bootstrap intervals for reuse, rigidity and entropy and reproduces the singleton fraction. It uses character transitions learned from the manuscript, and its matched-size type-to-token ratio remains about 15 percent high.

open.question: Can an independently specified token-formation process and local reuse rule match entropy and vocabulary growth together without learning the manuscript's character-transition table?
open.check: Freeze the generator and tune no parameters on test folios. Compare local reuse, conditional entropy, singleton fraction and type-to-token ratios at multiple matched token budgets.
